title: Design a Parking Lot (OOD)
prompt: Design the object model for a multi-level parking lot. It parks different vehicle types (motorcycle, car, bus/truck) into appropriately sized spots, issues a ticket on entry, and charges a fee on exit based on how long the vehicle stayed. Walk me through your classes, their relationships, and the key APIs. Sketch the class diagram on the whiteboard.
blurb: The canonical OOD warm-up — vehicle/spot hierarchies, spot allocation, ticketing, and pluggable pricing without a wall of if/else.

rubric.label: Requirements clarification
rubric.description: Nails down vehicle types, spot sizes, multi-level vs single, pricing model (hourly/flat/tiered), payment methods, and capacity queries before drawing classes.

rubric.label: Core entities
rubric.description: Identifies the right nouns: ParkingLot, Level, ParkingSpot, Vehicle, Ticket, Payment, and the entry/exit gates or terminals.

rubric.label: Class design
rubric.description: Clean fields/methods per class, Vehicle and ParkingSpot modeled as hierarchies or by size enum, encapsulated state (spot occupied/free) rather than public mutable data.

rubric.label: Relationships
rubric.description: Correct composition/aggregation: ParkingLot composes Levels, Level aggregates ParkingSpots, Ticket references Vehicle + Spot; multiplicities are explicit.

rubric.label: Design patterns
rubric.description: Strategy for pricing, Factory for spot/vehicle creation, optional Singleton for the lot; each justified, not name-dropped.

rubric.label: SOLID principles
rubric.description: Open/closed for new vehicle types and pricing rules; single-responsibility separation of allocation, ticketing, and payment.

rubric.label: API methods
rubric.description: Coherent public surface: parkVehicle, unpark/exit, computeFee, findSpot, availability; sensible return types and error signaling.

rubric.label: Extensibility
rubric.description: New vehicle types, EV charging spots, reserved/handicap spots, or a new pricing scheme drop in without editing existing allocation code.

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.description: Lot full, oversized vehicle in undersized spot, lost ticket, double-exit, spot freed on exit, partial-hour rounding.

rubric.label: Concurrency
rubric.description: Two entry gates racing for the last spot; atomic spot reservation; thread-safe availability counters.

rubric.label: Communication
rubric.description: Drives requirements first, thinks aloud, draws a legible class diagram, and responds to probes without thrashing the design.

functional_requirements: Support multiple vehicle types (motorcycle, car, bus/truck) mapped to spot sizes
Multiple levels, each with a set of spots of varying sizes
Assign a suitable free spot on entry and issue a ticket
Compute fee on exit based on duration and vehicle/spot type
Free the spot on exit and accept payment
Report real-time availability per level and per spot type
nonfunctional_requirements: Spot lookup and allocation should be fast (near O(1) amortized)
Thread-safe under concurrent entries/exits at multiple gates
Extensible to new vehicle types, pricing schemes, and spot features (EV, handicap)
No lost tickets / no double billing
clarifying_questions: What vehicle types must we support, and can a large vehicle occupy multiple/smaller spots?
Single lot or multiple levels? Do we track availability per level?
Pricing: flat, hourly, tiered by first-hour, or per-vehicle-type rates?
Payment methods — cash, card, both? Is payment part of scope or a separate service?
Do we support reservations, monthly passes, EV charging, or handicap spots?
What happens on a lost ticket — max daily charge?

core_classes.name: ParkingLot
core_classes.responsibility: Aggregate root; owns levels, coordinates park/unpark, exposes availability. Often a Singleton.

core_classes.name: Level
core_classes.responsibility: One floor; holds spots and answers allocation requests for a size.

core_classes.name: ParkingSpot
core_classes.responsibility: A single spot with a size and occupancy state; knows what it can fit.

core_classes.name: Vehicle (abstract)
core_classes.responsibility: Base type carrying license plate and required spot size; subclasses Motorcycle, Car, Truck.

core_classes.name: Ticket
core_classes.responsibility: Immutable record of a parked vehicle: spot, entry time, and enough info to bill and locate.

core_classes.name: PricingStrategy (interface)
core_classes.responsibility: Pluggable fee computation given ticket, exit time, and spot/vehicle type.

core_classes.name: SpotAssignmentStrategy (interface)
core_classes.responsibility: Pluggable policy for choosing among free spots (nearest-to-entrance, best-fit).

core_classes.name: Payment
core_classes.responsibility: Records amount, method, and status for an exit transaction.

relationships: ParkingLot composes Level (1..*) — levels do not outlive the lot (composition)
Ticket references one Vehicle and one ParkingSpot (association)
Vehicle is an inheritance hierarchy: Motorcycle/Car/Truck extend Vehicle (or use a SpotSize enum to avoid deep hierarchies)
ParkingLot has-a PricingStrategy and a SpotAssignmentStrategy (composition over inheritance)
SpotSize (SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE) is an enum shared by Vehicle and ParkingSpot

design_patterns.why: Swap hourly/flat/tiered pricing and nearest/best-fit allocation without touching the lot; keeps ParkingLot open for extension, closed for modification.

design_patterns.where: VehicleFactory / SpotFactory or a ParkingLot builder
design_patterns.why: Centralize construction of vehicle/spot subtypes so callers depend on abstractions, not concrete classes.
One physical lot; a single coordination point for availability — but discuss testability downsides and prefer dependency injection.

design_patterns.where: Availability display / gate signage subscribing to spot state changes
design_patterns.why: Decouple the display board from allocation logic.

apis: Ticket parkVehicle(Vehicle v) — allocates a spot or throws LotFullException
double unpark(Ticket t) — computes fee, frees the spot, returns amount due
state_transitions: Ticket/Session: ISSUED --vehicle exits, fee computed--> PENDING_PAYMENT --payment ok--> PAID (spot released on exit; ticket closed on PAID)
edge_cases: Lot or level full for the required size — return failure, try other levels first
Oversized vehicle: can a Truck use two adjacent large spots? Define policy explicitly
Lost ticket — fall back to max daily rate keyed by plate/entry-camera
Double exit / replayed ticket — idempotent unpark keyed by ticketId
Clock skew or exit before a full unit — rounding policy (round up to next hour)
Vehicle parked but never exits — long-stay reconciliation job
concurrency: Two gates racing for the last spot: guard allocation with per-level lock or a concurrent free-list (poll a thread-safe Deque) so assignment is atomic
Availability counters must be updated atomically with the spot state (AtomicInteger or under the same lock)
Prefer fine-grained locking per level/size bucket over one global lot lock to reduce contention
unpark must atomically compute fee + vacate to avoid a re-allocation seeing a stale occupied flag
extensibility: New vehicle type: add a subclass / map it to a SpotSize — no change to allocation
New pricing scheme (weekend surge, EV surcharge): implement PricingStrategy
EV charging spots: a SpotFeature/decorator or subtype of ParkingSpot with a canCharge flag
Reservations / monthly passes: a Reservation entity that pre-holds spots; allocation checks reserved pool first
Multiple lots / a chain: ParkingLot becomes one node; a LotManager routes vehicles

deep_dives.probe: How do you keep findSpot near O(1) instead of scanning every spot? What data structure holds the free spots per size?
Your fee logic has vehicle-type and duration branches. How do you model that without a growing if/else — where does Strategy fit and how does a new rate plug in?
A truck needs two adjacent spots. How does your model represent 'a booking that occupies multiple spots' and free them together?
Do you make Motorcycle/Car/Truck subclasses or use a SpotSize enum? What are the tradeoffs for extensibility and behavior?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions pricing or fee or rate
followup_bank.question: How do you support flat, hourly, and tiered pricing without editing the lot — Strategy injected into ParkingLot?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions if or switch or instanceof
followup_bank.question: That switch on vehicle type will grow. Can you replace it with polymorphism or a Strategy/Factory so new types don't touch this method?
Singleton makes testing and multi-lot support harder — how would you inject the lot instead, and when is Singleton actually justified here?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions find or search or scan
followup_bank.question: If you scan all spots to find a free one it's O(n). What structure gives you O(1) allocation per size bucket?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions thread or concurrent or lock
followup_bank.question: Two entry gates grab the last spot simultaneously — walk me through exactly where the lock or atomic op sits.

tradeoffs: Vehicle subclasses (richer behavior) vs SpotSize enum (fewer classes, simpler) — most designs favor the enum for size, subclasses only if behavior differs
Singleton lot (simple global access) vs injected instance (testable, multi-lot) — prefer injection
Best-fit allocation (space efficient) vs nearest-spot (better UX, simpler)
Per-level locks (more parallelism) vs one lot lock (simpler, contended)
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer first clarifies vehicle types, levels, and the pricing model, then models a small clean object graph: ParkingLot composes Levels, each Level aggregates ParkingSpots keyed into free-lists by SpotSize (enum), giving O(1) allocation. Vehicle carries a required SpotSize; a Ticket is an immutable entry record. Pricing and spot-selection are injected Strategy objects so hourly/flat/tiered rates and nearest/best-fit policies plug in under the open/closed principle, and a Factory builds vehicles/spots. The candidate makes spot state a proper FREE↔OCCUPIED transition, handles lot-full, lost-ticket, and double-exit edge cases, and addresses the last-spot race with a per-level lock or concurrent free-list. They proactively note extensibility to EV/handicap spots and reservations, and can justify enum-vs-hierarchy and Singleton-vs-injection tradeoffs rather than name-dropping patterns.

interviewer_notes: Let the candidate drive requirements before drawing classes; if they jump straight to code, ask them to enumerate entities first. Push hard on two things that separate mid from senior: (1) allocation complexity — if they scan all spots, ask for the O(1) free-list per size; (2) pricing without if/else — steer them to Strategy injected into the lot. Watch for over-engineering traps: a deep Vehicle inheritance tree when a SpotSize enum suffices, reaching for Singleton reflexively (probe testability), or premature Observer/event buses. If they finish early, throw the multi-spot truck or the EV-charging extension to test open/closed. Reserve the last few minutes for the last-spot concurrency race — make them point to exactly where the lock or atomic sits.
